messages.subject: Interaction Term with gdistsamp
parts:
For my thesis, I am analyzing a distance sampling data set of reptiles in different vegetation treatments and in two regions. I want to test an interaction term between my treatments and region. Can I do this with gdistsamp()?  I currently am using the following model.

m2 <- gdistsamp(~ (treatment-1) : region,   ~ 1, ~ tree.z,
                data = r.UMF, output="density", unitsOut = "ha", keyfun="halfnorm", mixture = "NB")

First, I believe ":"  is the right way to include an interaction between variables, is this right?

Second, any insight on why I am getting NA for my SE and Z?

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Interaction Term with gdistsamp
parts:
Dear Coral,

first, I think the Wilkinson-Rogers notation for linear models in unmarked is pretty much the same as what you have in other R functions, including lm() and glm(). The following toy data allows you to check out what such models mean (in your case I think you get what you want):

# Simulate two factors
trt <- as.factor(c(1,1,1,1,2,2,2,2))
region <- as.factor(c(1,1,2,2,1,1,2,2))

# Look at linear model structure of different models
model.matrix(~trt-1)
model.matrix(~region)
model.matrix(~trt * region)                # Main effects and interaction
model.matrix(~trt + region + trt:region)   # same
model.matrix(~(trt-1)*region)              # same, but different parameterization
model.matrix(~(trt-1):region)              # this is the same here, but again in a different parameterization

Second, all those NAs often mean that your model is too complex for your data. Can you show what you get when doing summary(umf), where umf is the name of the unmarked data frame ?

Thanks and best regards  --- Marc
